# Overview

This document is part of the Open Materials accompanying the book chapter

> Brandmaier, A. M. (in press). Towards reproducible data analysis of intensive
> longitudinal data in R. In T. Koch, T. Lischetzke, & J. Holtmann (Eds.),
> *Handbook of intensive longitudinal data analysis*. Routledge.

**Goal.** Demonstrate tools for reproducible research workflows with intensive
longitudinal data. This version is built with the
[`targets`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) package: all computations
(file loading, preprocessing, plotting, modeling) are **targets** defined in
`_targets.R`, and this report only *reads* their results. Running
`targets::tar_make()` re-runs exactly those steps whose code or inputs have
changed and then re-renders this page.

**Caveat.** The study has several phases, which are *not* modeled here. The
analysis only illustrates the workflow; we draw no substantive conclusions.


## Software and dependencies

Package versions are documented and can be restored with
[`renv`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/). Run `renv::init()` once and
`renv::snapshot()` after changing dependencies; collaborators then run
`renv::restore()`. The full session information is printed at the end of this
document.


## Data

Data from Kossakowski, Groot, Haslbeck, Borsboom, and Wichers (2017; *Journal of
Open Psychology Data, 5*(1), [doi:10.5334/jopd.29](https://doi.org/10.5334/jopd.29);
OSF: <https://osf.io/j4fg8>; CC BY 4.0). It is a single-case (N = 1)
experience-sampling study with about 10 beeps per day over 239 days and 50
items. The participant is male, aged 57, has a history of multiple episodes of
major depression, and had used antidepressants for the previous 8.5 years. He
monitored his momentary experiential states during a gradual discontinuation of
his antidepressant. Depressive symptoms were additionally assessed **weekly**
with the SCL-90-R depression subscale (variable `dep`).

# The pipeline

| Target | Step | Function (in `R/functions.R`) |
|---|---|---|
| `data_file` | file tracking (re-runs if the csv changes) | — |
| `raw_data` | file loading | `read_esm()` |
| `esm` | preprocessing: dates, sorting, day counter | `preprocess_esm()` |
| `beeps` | weekly rating carried forward (for plotting) | `make_beeps()` |
| `weekly` | one row per weekly assessment (for modeling) | `make_weekly()` |
| `fig_depression` | plotting | `make_depression_plot()` |
| `fig_file` | save figure as pdf | `save_plot()` |
| `model` | modeling | `fit_trend_model()` |
| `model_file` | save model as rds | `save_model()` |
| `report` | this html page | `tarchetypes::tar_render()` |

Package versions should additionally be pinned with
[`renv`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) (`renv::init()`, `renv::snapshot()`,
`renv::restore()`).

# Reading the results of the pipeline

`tar_read()` / `tar_load()` retrieve stored targets. `tar_render()` detects
these calls and makes this report depend on exactly these targets: if, e.g.,
only the plot code changes, only the plot and this page are rebuilt.

```{r load-targets}
library(targets)

tar_load(c(raw_data, esm, weekly, fig_depression, model))
```

```{r data-sizes}
n_beeps  <- nrow(raw_data)
n_weekly <- nrow(weekly)
```

The data contain `r n_beeps` beeps and `r n_weekly` weekly depression
assessments.

# Plot

The figure recreates the SCL-90-R depression subscale panel of Figure 1a in
Kossakowski et al. (2017). It was built by the target `fig_depression`; here we
simply display it. The dashed line is the linear trend of the weekly ratings,
i.e., the same data and model as reported below.

```{r fig-depression, fig.cap="Weekly SCL-90-R depression subscale (average item score) over the course of the study. The dashed line is the linear time trend estimated from the weekly assessments."}
fig_depression
```

The same figure was also saved as a pdf by the target `fig_file`
(`output/fig_depression.pdf`) and can be reused elsewhere without re-running
any code.

# Model

The target `model` fits a simple linear model that estimates the time trend of
the weekly depression ratings across **all** phases of the study, i.e., it
tests only the linear component of change over time:

```{r model-summary}
summary(model)
```

The fitted model is also stored on disk by the target `model_file`
(`output/model_esm.rds`).

# Reporting results with `cocoon`

The `cocoon` package formats model statistics so that they can be embedded
directly into text. `format_stats(model)` returns a formatted string for the
whole model; with `term`, the output is restricted to one term.

## Whole-model statistics

```{r format-model, results="asis"}
cat(cocoon::format_stats(model))
```

## Statistics for a single term

```{r format-term, results="asis"}
cat(cocoon::format_stats(model, term = "week"))
```

## Inline use in running text

The sentence below is written in R Markdown as
``Depression ratings changed linearly over time (`r knitr::inline_expr('cocoon::format_stats(model, term = "week")')`).``
and renders as:

> Depression ratings changed linearly over time
> (`r cocoon::format_stats(model, term = "week")`).

The overall fit can be reported likewise: `r cocoon::format_stats(model)`.

Because the numbers come from the `model` target, a change in the data, the
preprocessing, or the model automatically flows through `tar_make()` into the
figure, the tables, and every number in the text.
